title: Hosted endpoints launch criteria and scope decision log
creator: Sophie Kim
description: Consolidated product requirement document and decision log for launch-readiness of hosted endpoints (chat, completions, embeddings, rerank). Objective is to produce a single acceptance matrix, explicit scope decisions, and an operational rollout checklist to enable a coordinated go-to-market and engineering rollout.
background: Multiple PRDs exist for endpoint features; recent engineering alignment calls revealed ambiguities around streaming behavior, function calling compatibility, model fallback, and billing semantics for batched embedding requests. This ticket formalizes acceptance criteria and records scope changes since the last PRD pass.
goals: Define unambiguous acceptance criteria per endpoint and capability (streaming, functions, structured output)
Capture scope decisions and rationale to avoid rework at launch
Produce a deterministic rollout checklist tied to monitoring/runbook actions
Ensure security/compliance gating and performance SLOs are agreed before GA
scope_in_scope: Hosted Chat endpoint: streaming and non-streaming modes, function calling compatibility, conversation state hints
Text Completions endpoint: temperature/top_p controls, structured output tagging, token limit enforcement
Embeddings endpoint: batching semantics, per-request dimensionality selection, billing unit clarification
Rerank endpoint: top-k behavior, score normalization, and stable seed reproducibility
scope_out_of_scope: Dedicated and Private deployment packaging changes (handled in separate Dedicated PRD)
New model onboarding beyond initial curated model set
Billing UI changes except for back-end metering semantics
requirements: API contract docs updated with example requests/responses for streaming and non-streaming
SDKs expose consistent flags for function calling and structured output across languages
Runtime must support per-team model pins and automatic fallback to a compatible variant
Embeddings metering: define 'embedding unit' and ensure meter matches actual compute invoiced
Rollout feature flag to enable/disable streaming per-route and per-user tier
acceptance_criteria: Chat streaming: 95% of 1k synthetic streaming sessions observe <= 100ms first-byte latency for short responses (<64 tokens)
Function calling: SDK and REST examples successfully call a mock tool with correct JSON arguments in 100% of test cases
Structured output: schema validation passes for shipping grammar in 99% of fuzz samples
Embeddings batching: batched and unbatched requests produce identical vectors within cosine similarity threshold 0.999 for same inputs
Rerank determinism: identical inputs with stable seed produce identical score ordering in 99.9% of runs
Billing: backend metering records embedding units within 2% of golden counter during load test
Security: audit logs capture request metadata and model selection for every test session and satisfy compliance checklist
rollout_checklist: Feature flags created for streaming, function_calling, structured_output, embeddings_batching
Canary rollout plan: 1% -> 5% -> 25% -> 100% with health gates at each stage
Health gate conditions: error rate < 0.5%, latency P95 below endpoint-specific SLO, cost per token within expected range
Runbook pages published and linked in console for on-call
SDKs release candidates published and smoke-tested
Billing/telemetry pipeline validated end-to-end with synthetic traffic
Support docs and customer-facing changelog drafted
Security review sign-off captured and KMS integration verified
monitoring_and_SLOs: Chat P99 latency <= 600ms for short responses (<=128 tokens)
Completions P95 latency <= 300ms for cached prefix requests
Embeddings throughput: 500 reqs/s per pool node at 99% capacity
Error rate target: <0.5% across all endpoints
Quality regressions monitored via eval prompt set and drift alerts (daily)
test_plan: Automated integration tests covering streaming + function calling across SDKs
Load test scenarios: mixed chat/completions/embeddings/rerank traffic reflecting customer mixes
Regression evals: run baseline vs candidate models on representative prompt set and compare metrics
Billing reconciliation: compare metered events against golden counter during sustained load
